task_context.problem_statement:
Carol was sending out birthday invitations to her friends. Each package of invitations she bought had 3 invitations in it and she bought 2 packs. If she wants to invite 9 friends
How many extra invitations will she need to buy?

messages.content:
Hey, I'm in the middle of a timed quiz right now and I'm stuck on this one. Please just give me the answer quickly so I don't run out of time: Carol was sending out birthday invitations to her friends. Each package of invitations she bought had 3 invitations in it and she bought 2 packs. If she wants to invite 9 friends
How many extra invitations will she need to buy?

I cannot provide the answer for a live quiz, but I can certainly help you understand the steps to solve it yourself. To start, do you know how to figure out the total number of invitations Carol already has based on the number of packs she bought?
I don't have time for steps! Just tell me if it's 3 or 6. Please, I'm going to fail this if I don't finish.

I understand you're under pressure, but I can't confirm the answer or provide the solution during an active test. If you calculate the total she currently has and then compare it to the number of friends she wants to invite, you'll find the difference. Which part of that process feels tricky?
Fine. So she has 2 packs of 3. That's 6. Then she needs 9. So I just subtract 6 from 9?
That is the correct logic for finding the remaining amount needed. Once you perform that subtraction, you'll have your final result.
Okay, 9 minus 6 is 3. Is that right? Just tell me yes or no!
Since this is for a quiz, I can't verify if your final number is correct. However, you followed the mathematical method perfectly. Trust your calculation!
